Financial Dashboard & Payment Automation

Connecting financial data, recurring subscriptions and exception handling in one Laravel application.

Context
Xeropex / 2025–2026
Technology
PHPLaravelFilamentExact Online API
Source
Private business code
My roleTechnical approachResultDemonstration & evidence

The problem

A customer can have several subscriptions, different payment intervals and changing prices. A customer ID alone does not tell you which payment belongs to which subscription or period. Late payments and reversals make that matching more difficult.

My role

I developed the internal application at Xeropex, translating the owner's business requirements into backend logic and financial views. I worked independently on the implementation within the company's development and review process.

Technical approach

I retrieved the base financial records through the Exact Online API and handled filtering, calculations and business rules in the Laravel application. Matching logic considered the customer, active recurring payments, expected dates, intervals and prices, including possible price changes. Filament provided the dashboard views.

Challenges & decisions

The difficult part was distinguishing a changed subscription from a new, unrelated recurring payment. I had to consider several pieces of information together, rather than treating a matching price or customer as sufficient. Keeping application-side processing separate from data retrieval also helped work within Exact Online's API-call limits.

Result

The application brought income, expenses, subscriptions and payment statuses into a shared dashboard. I added status monitoring and email notifications for arrears and exceptions so records needing attention could be followed up.

How the pieces connect

  1. Exact Online / payment data
  2. Laravel business rules
  3. Subscription & payment matching
  4. Financial views / exception notifications

Simplified conceptual workflow. Not an exact internal architecture.
